newsitem.title: INDIA: Calcutta prices down on sell-out by FIIs.
newsitem.headline: Calcutta prices down on sell-out by FIIs.

text.p: Share prices suffered at the Calcutta bourse on Monday after foreign institutional investors (FIIs) sold blue chips in thin trade, brokers said.

They said overall trading was very thin and restricted to just a few blue chips which faced steady selling pressures from foreign funds. FIIs liquidated large lots of scrips and there was no buying during the day, brokers said.
The BSE was closed for the Hindu festival of the elephant-headed god Ganesh, and most of the selling was concentrated on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and the Calcutta Stock Exchange (CSE).
Technically, the markets are very weak, analysts said.
"The technical charts are showing the head-and-shoulder formation which is interpreted as one of the worst long-term bearish signals," said an analyst with brokers C. Makertich.

"Every foreign fund is selling out to make an exit. If current trends persist there may be a flight of capital from Indian secondary markets which means that outflow of funds would be more than inflow of foreign investments in Indian secondary markets for equities," the analyst said.
Brokers said selling pressures would mount and blue-chips suffer another setback once the Bombay bourse reopens after the festival.
